image_description: A grey whale tail fluke (caudal fin) emerging vertically from the ocean surface during a dive. The flukes are dark grey/black with white mottling on the underside and trailing edges. Water is splashing off the right side of the tail. The background consists of calm blue ocean water and a clear sky horizon.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Head is relatively short with arched rostrum and two blowholes on top.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The head is completely submerged and not visible in the frame; only the tail flukes are shown.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Skin is mottled grey to greyish-black with distinctive white patches from barnacles and whale lice.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The visible skin on the tail flukes exhibits the characteristic dark grey base color with irregular white mottling/scarring consistent with barnacle/cyamid patterns found on grey whales.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: No dorsal fin present; multiple dorsal knuckles along posterior back.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The dorsal ridge/knuckles are located anterior to the tail and are submerged/not visible in this specific 'fluke-up' dive shot.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Robust spindle-shaped body of enormous proportions.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The majority of the body is submerged; only the caudal peduncle and flukes are visible, making full body shape assessment impossible.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Skin is mottled grey with white patches created by barnacles.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: Consistent with the Head checkpoint; the visible tail surface shows accurate mottling texture and coloration.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Baleen plates are cream-colored, densely packed in numerous rows along each side.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: Baleen plates are located inside the mouth/head, which is not visible.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Flippers (pectoral fins) are broad and paddle-shaped, remarkably elongated relative to body size.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: Pectoral fins are located on the sides of the body and are not visible in this rear-view tail shot.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Tail flukes are broad with smooth trailing edge and central notch.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The image clearly displays broad tail flukes with a distinct central notch (median cleft) and relatively smooth trailing edges, matching grey whale anatomy.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Skin texture is rough with callosities.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The surface texture appears uneven and mottled, consistent with the rough skin and callosities typical of the species, rather than smooth shark-like skin.
